Solicitation and Advertising
Agents must comply with the Telephone Consumer Protection Act Do-Not-Call provisions and with the CAN-SPAM Act for electronic marketing. Calls to prospective clients are permitted only under the exceptions established by law, for example when returning an inquiry within three months, when the agent has prior agency or brokerage relationship within the prior 18 months, or when the recipient has given prior written consent. All advertising, including social media posts, print, and digital content, must conspicuously include Elm & Ivy Properties’ name and logo and the name and license number or contact information of the supervising broker or the agent as required by Florida law. Advertising must not mislead consumers or omit required disclosures.
Confidentiality and IT Use
Agents must protect confidential information of Elm & Ivy Properties and its clients at all times. Confidential information includes client motivation, financial qualifications, negotiated terms, firm strategies, and unpublished marketing plans. Agents must not discuss confidential client or firm information in public or in locations where the conversation may be overheard. Electronic information must be secured through strong passwords, approved storage locations, and adherence to any IT security procedures established by the firm. IT resources such as email, voicemail, internet, and company devices are provided primarily for business use, and Elm & Ivy Properties reserves the right to monitor usage. Associates should have no expectation of privacy when using company systems. Inappropriate use of IT resources, including accessing or distributing sexually explicit material, hacking, or using unauthorized accounts, is prohibited and may result in discipline or termination.
Termination of Affiliation
Upon termination of the association with Elm & Ivy Properties, the agent must immediately return all company property, including manuals, equipment, keys, access codes, and Elm & Ivy Properties records. All transaction files, records, and proprietary information in the agent’s possession that relate to the firm’s business must be returned unless alternate arrangements are documented in a written separation agreement.
